# Blobbies

> Deterministic, cute SVG avatars from a name. Zero dependencies. The same name
> always produces the same avatar, on every platform.

The decisions that make an avatar (the two letters used as eyes, colour, egg
shape, mood, blush, tilt) are a pure function of the name and live in
`packages/core`. Every framework binding is a thin renderer over those
decisions. A shared conformance file proves the renderers agree.

## Packages

- `blobbies` — core. Hash, initials, trait decisions, scene, SVG string, data URI, DOM motion, CLI. Framework-agnostic, zero dependencies.
- `@blobbies/react` — `<Avatar>`, `<AvatarPicker>`, `useAvatarMotion`. Peer: `react >= 18`.
- `@blobbies/element` — `<blobbies-avatar>` web component. Works in every web framework and plain HTML.
- `@blobbies/react-native` — `<Avatar>` over `react-native-svg`. Peers: `react-native`, `react-native-svg`, `react-native-reanimated`.
- `Blobbies` (Swift) — engine, SVG renderer and native `BlobbiesAvatar` SwiftUI view. SPM, no dependencies.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): install, quick start, every option with examples.
- [Platform plan](docs/PLATFORMS.md): how Blobbies works on every platform, and how to add one.
- [Agent guide](AGENTS.md): repo commands, the rules, the traps.
- [Core README](packages/core/README.md): the string renderer and motion runtime.
- [React README](packages/react/README.md): the components and the picker parts.

## Machine-readable data

- [manifest.json](packages/core/manifest.json): every shape, mood, colour and layout value as JSON. Use this to port Blobbies to another language.
- [avatar-conformance.json](packages/core/fixtures/avatar-conformance.json): 24 known-correct input/output cases. A port must reproduce these byte-for-byte.

## Core API (`blobbies`)

```ts
import { renderAvatarSvg, renderAvatarBody, avatarDataUri, resolveAvatar } from 'blobbies';
import { attachAvatarMotion } from 'blobbies/motion';

renderAvatarSvg(name: string, options?: AvatarOptions): string
renderAvatarBody(name: string, options?: AvatarOptions): ResolvedAvatar
avatarDataUri(name: string, options?: AvatarOptions): string
resolveAvatar(name: string, options?: AvatarOptions): ResolvedAvatar
attachAvatarMotion(element: SVGSVGElement, options?: MotionOptions): () => void
```

`resolveAvatar` returns `{ name, letters, prefix, traits, body, blink }` where
`traits` is the portable set of decisions.

Enumerable options (see `manifest.json` for the values):

- `shape`: `tall | wide | squat | round | mid`
- `expression`: 22 moods, e.g. `smile | smirk | wink | angry | cat | shy`
- `color`: any CSS colour, or a name from the built-in palette
- `blush`: boolean
- `variant`: number — a different body for the same name; `0` is the original.

Object options: `size`, `rounded`, `title`, `className`, `palette`, `tilt`,
`animate` (`false | 'blink' | 'follow' | 'all'`), `blinkInterval`, `follow`,
`followRange`, `smoothing`, `idleTimeout`, `paused`, `respectReducedMotion`,
`wink`, `glance`, `surprise`.

## CLI

```bash
npx blobbies render "Sourav Nanda" > avatar.svg
npx blobbies render "Ira" --expression wink --color sky --animate all
npx blobbies shapes
npx blobbies expressions
npx blobbies palette
npx blobbies manifest
```

## Rules for tools and agents

- Never re-implement the algorithm in a binding; change `packages/core` instead.
- Never edit `manifest.json` or `avatar-conformance.json` by hand — regenerate them.
- `variant: 0` must keep producing the original avatar forever.
- A port is correct when it reproduces `avatar-conformance.json` byte-for-byte.
